title: On the largest chromatic number of $F$-free hypergraphs
summary: Given a hypergraph $F$, what is the largest chromatic number that an $F$-free hypergraph can have? In the case of graphs, this question is easy to answer: the chromatic number is unbounded if $F$ contains a cycle, and the largest chromatic number of $F$-free graphs is $k-1$ if $F$ is a forest on $k$ vertices. The situation is more complicated for hypergraphs. The strong coloring of a hypergraph is a coloring of the vertices such that every hyperedge is rainbow.
